WITH ibd_persons AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT co.person_id
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON co.condition_concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (
    SELECT concept_id FROM omop.concept

      AND standard_concept = 'S'
  )
),
eim AS (
  SELECT 'Arthritis / arthropathy' AS category, ARRAY['Rheumatoid arthritis','Ankylosing spondylitis','Psoriatic arthritis','Arthropathy','Spondyloarthropathy','Sacroiliitis'] AS names UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Axial spondyloarthritis', ARRAY['Ankylosing spondylitis','Sacroiliitis'] UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Psoriasis', ARRAY['Psoriasis'] UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Primary sclerosing cholangitis', ARRAY['Primary sclerosing cholangitis'] UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Uveitis / iritis', ARRAY['Uveitis','Iritis','Episcleritis','Scleritis'] UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Erythema nodosum', ARRAY['Erythema nodosum'] UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Pyoderma gangrenosum', ARRAY['Pyoderma gangrenosum'] UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Venous thromboembolism', ARRAY['Venous thrombosis','Pulmonary embolism','Deep venous thrombosis'] UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Anemia', ARRAY['Anemia','Iron deficiency anemia'] UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Osteoporosis', ARRAY['Osteoporosis','Osteopenia']
)
SELECT e.category,
       COUNT(DISTINCT co.person_id) AS n_patients,
       ROUND(100.0*COUNT(DISTINCT co.person_id)/27774,2) AS pct_of_ibd
FROM eim e
JOIN omop.concept c
  ON c.concept_name = ANY(e.names) AND c.standard_concept = 'S' AND c.domain_id='Condition'
JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.ancestor_concept_id = c.concept_id
JOIN omop.condition_occurrence co ON co.condition_concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
JOIN ibd_persons ip ON ip.person_id = co.person_id
GROUP BY e.category
ORDER BY n_patients DESC;

content.text: This is SQL Server (T-SQL), not PostgreSQL — no `ARRAY` type. Let me rewrite using standard T-SQL with a lookup of condition categories via `LIKE` on descendant concept names.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH ibd_persons AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT co.person_id
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON co.condition_concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
  JOIN omop.concept anc ON anc.concept_id = ca.ancestor_concept_id
  WHERE anc.concept_name IN ('Crohn''s disease','Ulcerative colitis','Inflammatory bowel disease')
    AND anc.standard_concept = 'S'
),
pt_cond AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ip.person_id, anc.concept_name AS cond
  FROM ibd_persons ip
  JOIN omop.condition_occurrence co ON co.person_id = ip.person_id
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
  JOIN omop.concept anc ON anc.concept_id = ca.ancestor_concept_id
  WHERE anc.standard_concept = 'S' AND anc.domain_id = 'Condition'
)
SELECT category,
       COUNT(DISTINCT person_id) AS n_patients,
       CAST(ROUND(100.0*COUNT(DISTINCT person_id)/27774.0,2) AS DECIMAL(5,2)) AS pct_of_ibd
FROM (
  SELECT person_id,
    CASE
      WHEN cond IN ('Rheumatoid arthritis','Ankylosing spondylitis','Psoriatic arthritis','Spondyloarthropathy','Sacroiliitis','Arthropathy') THEN 'Inflammatory arthritis / spondyloarthritis'
      WHEN cond = 'Psoriasis' THEN 'Psoriasis'
      WHEN cond = 'Primary sclerosing cholangitis' THEN 'Primary sclerosing cholangitis'
      WHEN cond IN ('Uveitis','Iritis','Episcleritis','Scleritis') THEN 'Ocular (uveitis/episcleritis)'
      WHEN cond = 'Erythema nodosum' THEN 'Erythema nodosum'
      WHEN cond = 'Pyoderma gangrenosum' THEN 'Pyoderma gangrenosum'
      WHEN cond IN ('Venous thrombosis','Pulmonary embolism','Deep venous thrombosis of lower limb','Deep vein thrombosis') THEN 'Venous thromboembolism'
      WHEN cond IN ('Anemia','Iron deficiency anemia','Anemia due to chronic disorder') THEN 'Anemia'
      WHEN cond IN ('Osteoporosis','Osteopenia') THEN 'Osteoporosis / osteopenia'
    END AS category
  FROM pt_cond
) x
WHERE category IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY n_patients DESC;

## IBD extraintestinal comorbidities (clinical cohort, n = 27,774)

Most frequent extraintestinal/associated comorbidities among IBD patients in the EHR:

| Comorbidity | Patients | % of IBD |
|---|---|---|
| Anemia | 9,580 | 34.5% |
| Inflammatory arthritis / spondyloarthritis | 8,669 | 31.2% |
| Osteoporosis / osteopenia | 2,825 | 10.2% |
| Venous thromboembolism | 2,138 | 7.7% |
| Psoriasis | 1,010 | 3.6% |
| Ocular (uveitis/episcleritis) | 536 | 1.9% |
| Primary sclerosing cholangitis | 469 | 1.7% |
| Pyoderma gangrenosum | 225 | 0.8% |
| Erythema nodosum | 202 | 0.7% |

Anemia and inflammatory arthritis dominate. The classic "immune-mediated" EIMs (arthritis, psoriasis, uveitis, PSC, PG, erythema nodosum) cluster together, which is the group most likely to share signaling with gut inflammation.

## Immune signaling that plausibly underlies the shared EIMs

*Note: the knowledge-graph endpoint timed out repeatedly this session and returned nothing, so the mechanisms below are from established immunology, not KG-derived. I can retry the graph later if it recovers.*

- **IL-23 / Th17 axis (IL-23R → RORγt → IL-17A/F, IL-22).** The strongest shared thread. Gut-primed Th17 cells traffic to joints, skin, and eye; explains why axial spondyloarthritis, psoriasis, and uveitis co-segregate with IBD and why IL-23/IL-17-directed biologics (ustekinumab, risankizumab) treat several of these together. *IL23R* is a shared GWAS locus across IBD, AS, and psoriasis.
- **TNF-α.** Common effector across gut, joint, skin, and eye inflammation; anti-TNF efficacy in CD/UC plus AS, PsA, uveitis, and pyoderma gangrenosum reflects a shared pathway.
- **Gut–lymphocyte trafficking (α4β7/MAdCAM-1, CCR9/CCL25).** Aberrant homing of mucosal effector cells to extraintestinal sites is a leading model for EIMs.
- **Neutrophil-driven / innate (IL-1β, IL-8, IL-36) inflammation.** Underlies the neutrophilic dermatoses — pyoderma gangrenosum and erythema nodosum.
- **Anemia** is mostly *mechanistically distinct*: iron-deficiency from chronic GI blood loss plus **IL-6 → hepcidin**-driven anemia of inflammation (functional iron restriction) — a cytokine link but not a shared autoimmune target.
- **VTE** reflects an inflammation-driven **prothrombotic state** (IL-6/TNF raising fibrinogen, platelet activation, endothelial dysfunction) rather than shared adaptive immunity.
- **PSC** has a distinct immunogenetic profile (HLA-associated, gut-liver lymphocyte homing via aberrant MAdCAM-1/CCL25 in liver) and, unlike the others, responds poorly to the same biologics.

Bottom line: an **IL-23/Th17 → IL-17/22 + TNF** program, coupled with **aberrant mucosal lymphocyte homing**, is the most likely shared immune driver of the immune-mediated EIMs (arthritis/spondyloarthritis, psoriasis, uveitis, neutrophilic skin lesions), whereas anemia, VTE, and osteoporosis arise largely from downstream/systemic consequences of chronic inflammation.
